references.text: In the parable of the sower, Jesus describes those who hear the word and hold fast to it with "a noble and good heart" and bear fruit "with perseverance" (ὑπομονή). The same connection between perseverance and preserving one's life/soul. [ref:Luk 8:15|Luke 8:15]

Jesus teaches that whoever tries to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses it will preserve it. This illuminates the paradox in Luke 21:19 about gaining one's soul through patient perseverance. [ref:Luk 17:33|Luke 17:33]
The author of Hebrews urges perseverance (ὑπομονή) to obtain what is promised, which directly reflects Jesus' words about winning the soul through perseverance. [ref:Heb 10:36|Hebrews 10:36]

James writes that the testing of faith produces perseverance (ὑπομονή), and that perseverance must lead to a complete work. The same theme of perseverance under trials as in Luke 21:19. [ref:Jak 1:3-4|James 1:3-4]

Paul writes that tribulation produces perseverance, perseverance produces character, and character produces hope. The connection between suffering and perseverance illuminates Jesus' words. [ref:Rom 5:3-4|Romans 5:3-4]

Paul speaks of those who by perseverance (ὑπομονή) in good works seek glory, honor, and immortality—eternal life. Perseverance is linked to winning eternal life, as in Luke 21:19. [ref:Rom 2:7|Romans 2:7]

Jesus promises the church in Philadelphia that because they have held fast to his word about perseverance (ὑπομονή), he will keep them from the hour of trial. Perseverance leads to preservation, as in Luke 21:19. [ref:Åp 3:10|Revelation 3:10]

The call to run with perseverance (ὑπομονή) the race set before us, fixing our eyes on Jesus. The theme of perseverance under persecution and trials is shared with Luke 21:19. [ref:Heb 12:1|Hebrews 12:1]

The immediate context where Jesus predicts persecution, imprisonment, and hatred for his name's sake, but assures that not a hair on their heads will be lost. The perseverance in verse 19 is the answer to these trials. [ref:Luk 21:12-18|Luke 21:12-18]
Jesus says that whoever endures to the end will be saved. A direct parallel to the thought in Luke 21:19 that perseverance leads to salvation/preservation of the soul. [ref:Matt 10:22|Matthew 10:22]
In the eschatological discourse in Matthew, Jesus again says that whoever endures to the end will be saved—a close parallel to Luke 21:19. [ref:Matt 24:13|Matthew 24:13]
